documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

66 y/o retired farmer establishing care after his longtime PCP retired.

COPD: told years ago it was "severe." Several hospital stays for flare-ups over the last decade, none in the past year by his account. Has seen a pulmonary group on and off. Uses tiotropium every morning and the fluticasone/salmeterol disk twice a day "most days"; albuterol a few times a day, more in humid weather. Breathless walking up to the barn or carrying feed, fine on the flat at his own pace. Chronic morning cough with some white sputum. No oxygen at home.

Tobacco: 1 pack a day since his mid-20s, so roughly 40 pack-years. Has quit "a dozen times" for a few weeks each. Not interested in a quit date today.
Alcohol: 3-4 drinks most evenings, beer or rye. AUDIT-C 6.

Also mentions a sore on his lower lip that "won't heal," there for a few months, gets a crust, picks at it. Spent his life outdoors without a hat most days.

PMH: COPD. PSH: none.
Meds: tiotropium 18 mcg inh daily; fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 1 inh BID; albuterol MDI PRN.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
FH: father had COPD and lung cancer; mother had heart disease.
SH: divorced, lives alone on the home farm, leased the fields out when he retired. Drives.

EXAM: thin man, mildly short of breath conversing after the walk from the lot. Prolonged expiration, scattered faint wheezes, distant breath sounds. Heart regular, no murmur. No JVD. No edema. Lower lip vermilion: about 1 cm crusted firm lesion, slightly raised. No palpable neck nodes.

A/P
1. COPD, severe, GOLD D by history. Continue current triple therapy. Inhaler technique reviewed; he was skipping the evening dose of the disk. Requesting old records and PFTs from the prior office.
2. Tobacco: strongly advised quitting. Discussed patch/gum, varenicline. Declines for now; will revisit.
3. Lower lip lesion, persistent: needs biopsy. Dermatology referral placed.
4. Alcohol above recommended limits: brief counseling given.
5. Health maintenance: labs today (CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, hep C, HIV). Prior records to confirm colonoscopy and vaccines. Flu shot when the high-dose arrives.

PHQ-2: 0.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Bianchi, your bloodwork from Tuesday came back fine: kidney and liver tests normal, blood counts normal, cholesterol in a reasonable range, sugar (A1c) normal. Hepatitis C and HIV screens negative. Nothing to change. The dermatology office should be calling you to schedule the lip appointment.

documents.title: Prior PCP records
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received by fax from the patient's former primary care office (48 pages). Abstracted:
- COPD on triple inhaled therapy for several years; spirometry in 2017 showed severe obstruction.
- Screening colonoscopy 2016: no polyps, repeat in 10 years.
- PPSV23 given 10/2018. Flu shots most years.
- Ongoing smoking counseling documented at most visits.
Original pages scanned under Media. Forwarded to PCP.

conditions.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of skin of lip

reports.text: Specimen: lower lip vermilion, shave biopsy. Microscopic: invasive cords of atypical squamous epithelium with keratin pearl formation extending into the dermis.
reports.conclusion: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma, keratinizing type, lower lip. Peripheral and deep margins involved by tumor.

documents.title: Dermatology consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION LETTER
Date of visit: 11/09/2020
Re: Richard Bianchi, DOB 10/08/1953
Referred by: primary care

Thank you for this referral. Mr. Bianchi reports a sore on the lower lip that has been there several months and has slowly gotten bigger. He denies weight loss, fevers or night sweats. He farmed his whole working life, mostly without sun protection, and smokes about a pack a day, which he has done for 40 years.

Exam: on the vermilion border of the lower lip there is a firm, ulcerated 1 cm nodule with a small area of crust. Cervical and submandibular chains without palpable adenopathy. No other suspicious lesions on the face, scalp, neck or arms on today's check; scattered solar lentigines.

Procedure: shave biopsy of the lip lesion under local anesthesia.

Pathology (finalized 11/11): invasive keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma with keratin pearls.

Assessment: cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, lower lip.
Plan: surgical excision with our dermatologic surgery team, scheduled 11/30. Sun protection and lip balm with SPF reviewed. We will follow him for skin checks.

Medications reviewed: tiotropium, fluticasone/salmeterol, albuterol. NKDA.

reports.text: Specimen: lower lip, wedge excision, oriented. Residual invasive keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma at the prior biopsy site. Margins: all margins free of tumor.

documents.author: dermatology

OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGIC SURGERY - PROCEDURE REPORT (received by fax)
Date of procedure: 11/30/2020
Procedure: excision of squamous cell carcinoma, lower lip vermilion, with layered closure.
Anesthesia: local.
Findings: healed biopsy site with residual firm induration, excised with margin and closed primarily.
Pathology 12/02: residual SCC, margins clear.
Complications: none. EBL minimal.
Allergies: NKDA.
Plan: suture removal 1 week; skin check in 6 months then yearly. Patient instructed on wound care and sun protection.

documents.title: lip and covid shot
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Stitches came out friday, lip is healing ok just numb in one spot. The skin doc says they got it all. Question - when can I get the covid vaccine with my lungs? My neighbor says the pharmacies are taking names.

documents.title: RE: lip and covid shot
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Glad to hear it, and the pathology report reached us: clean margins. Numbness at the scar often improves over months.

You will be in an early group for the vaccine because of your age and lungs. The state is rolling it out by phases; I would sign up with the pharmacy as your neighbor said, and we will message patients when we know more.

orders.reason: progressive hoarseness and dysphagia in a smoker, rule out laryngeal malignancy

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: voice changes

Voice has been getting rougher since late January. Initially blamed it on a cold, but it never came back. Now hoarse all day. Sometimes feels food (bread, meat) catch on the way down and a sense of a lump in his throat; liquids fine. Mild throat ache. No coughing up blood, no fevers, no night sweats, weight stable by his account. Still smoking 1 ppd; drinks most evenings. Breathing at baseline.

Lip healed, follows with dermatology.

Meds: tiotropium daily, fluticasone/salmeterol BID, albuterol PRN.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Exam: voice hoarse and husky. Oropharynx without visible lesion, no thrush. Neck supple, no palpable mass or node, thyroid not enlarged. Lungs with diffuse decreased breath sounds and prolonged expiration, no crackles. Heart regular. Lip scar well healed.

A/P
Hoarseness >2 months with intermittent solid-food dysphagia in a heavy smoker and drinker. Needs direct visualization of the larynx soon. Urgent ENT referral placed; called the ENT office and they will see him 4/28. Told him to call if he has trouble swallowing liquids, breathing noise, or coughs up blood.
Smoking: talked again about stopping, especially now. He will "think about it."

reports.text: Specimen: left true vocal cord, biopsy. Fragments of squamous mucosa with invasive squamous cell carcinoma.
reports.conclusion: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma, left true vocal cord.

documents.title: Otolaryngology consultation
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OTOLARYNGOLOGY - HEAD AND NECK SURGERY
New patient consultation, seen 4/28/2021. Letter dictated after pathology returned.

HPI: 67-year-old man referred for three months of worsening hoarseness and intermittent difficulty swallowing. He notes a mild discomfort in the throat and the feeling of a lump when he swallows solids. About five months ago he had a squamous cell carcinoma of the lower lip excised by dermatology. No fevers, sweats or unintended weight loss.

Habits: smokes 1 pack per day; 3 to 4 alcoholic drinks most evenings.

Meds: tiotropium, fluticasone/salmeterol, albuterol. Allergies: none known.

Exam: husky voice. Mild tenderness over the anterior neck, nothing visible. No palpable cervical masses. Laryngoscopy: irregular exophytic lesion on the left true vocal cord; that cord moves less than the right. Biopsy taken in clinic under topical anesthesia; tolerated well.

Pathology (5/3): invasive squamous cell carcinoma.

Impression: squamous cell carcinoma of the left true vocal cord.
Plan: CT neck and chest with contrast for staging, then discussion at our tumor board and surgical planning. Smoking cessation is strongly advised and he was given the state quitline number.

reports.text: Technique: axial images through the neck after IV contrast. Soft tissue thickening and enhancing mass along the left true vocal cord. No cervical lymphadenopathy by size or morphology. Thyroid, salivary glands and airway otherwise unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Left true vocal cord mass. No cervical nodal disease.

reports.text: Technique: contrast-enhanced axial images of the chest. Lungs hyperinflated. No pulmonary nodule or mass. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: Hyperinflated lungs. No evidence of intrathoracic metastatic disease.

documents.title: Call with patient re: diagnosis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called him after the ENT letter and CT reports came in. He already knew the biopsy result. CT shows no spread to the neck nodes or lungs, which ENT told him is good news. Surgery being planned for early June.

He sounded flat. Asked how he is doing: "Can't say I'm surprised." Not drinking more than usual, sleeping ok. Again offered help with quitting: nicotine patch or varenicline. Declined, says he has cut to "about a pack." Told him smoking after treatment raises the chance of another cancer and he should call any time. He will.

documents.title: Dermatology follow-up
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
6-month skin check after excision of lower lip SCC. Scar on the lower lip well healed, no nodularity. Full skin exam: solar lentigines and sun damage over the forearms and face; no suspicious lesions today. No cervical adenopathy.
Plan: yearly skin exams, broad-brim hat, SPF lip balm. Aware of upcoming laryngeal surgery.

events.reason: Partial laryngectomy for left vocal cord carcinoma

reports.text: Specimen: left partial laryngectomy, oriented, with separately submitted margin biopsies. Invasive squamous cell carcinoma involving the left true vocal cord. All surgical margins and margin biopsies negative for carcinoma.
reports.conclusion: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma, left true vocal cord; margins negative.

documents.title: Discharge summary - partial laryngectomy
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 6/9/2021, discharged 6/11/2021. Service: Otolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery.

Diagnosis: squamous cell carcinoma, left true vocal cord.
Procedure 6/9: direct laryngoscopy with frozen-section biopsies and partial laryngectomy. Frozen sections clear.

Course: extubated in the OR. Overnight monitoring for airway, uneventful. Pain controlled with oral medication. Swallow evaluation POD1: safe for soft solids and thin liquids with small sips. Continued home inhalers; one albuterol neb for wheeze the first night. Ambulating, voiding.

Final pathology: invasive SCC, all margins negative. Tumor board recommendation: no adjuvant radiation; surveillance.

Discharge meds: home inhalers unchanged; acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: ENT clinic 4 weeks. PCP 1-2 weeks.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Two weeks out from partial laryngectomy. Voice weak and breathy, tires by afternoon. Swallowing soft food and most solids now, slower. Neck sore early on, now just tight. Using acetaminophen once in a while. Breathing about as usual. Smoking "less," maybe half a pack, though he admits it creeps up.

Path reviewed with him: margins negative, no radiation planned.

O: breathy, soft voice. Neck incisions healing, no erythema or drainage. Lungs: decreased BS throughout, no crackles. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
1. SCC left vocal cord s/p partial laryngectomy. Recovering. ENT 7/7.
2. COPD: stable on current inhalers.
3. Tobacco: encouraged him to keep cutting down to zero; offered patch again. Declines.
Return in fall for wellness visit.

documents.title: Otolaryngology follow-up
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OTOLARYNGOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Seen 7/7/2021, four weeks after left partial laryngectomy. Healing well; flexible laryngoscopy shows the operative bed mucosalized, airway adequate. Voice breathy as expected. Swallowing without aspiration symptoms.

Final margins were negative and the tumor board did not recommend adjuvant therapy.

Surveillance plan: flexible laryngoscopy in clinic every 3 to 4 months for two years, then every 6 to 12 months; CT neck and chest yearly for three years. We once again urged him to stop smoking.

documents.author: PCP

MEDICARE ANNUAL WELLNESS VISIT (initial)

Interval: lower lip SCC excised 11/2020, clear margins, derm skin check 6/2021 clean. Left vocal cord SCC: partial laryngectomy 6/9/21, margins negative, no adjuvant therapy; ENT surveillance ongoing, most recent scope clear. Voice still breathy but stronger than in June.

COPD: stable, no flares this year. Same three inhalers. Gets winded with barn chores.

Functional: independent with ADLs and IADLs. Lives alone, drives, does his own shopping. No falls. Hearing ok in quiet rooms. Home has stairs to the bedroom, manages.
Cognition: clock draw and 3-word recall normal.
PHQ-2: 0. AUDIT-C: 6 - still 3-4 drinks most nights; discussed cutting back, he is not keen.
Tobacco: still ~1 ppd. Counseled. Declines meds.

Advance directive: will think about a health care proxy; form given.

Exam: BP fine. Breathy voice. Healed neck scars. Lungs: decreased breath sounds, prolonged expiratory phase. Heart regular, no murmur. No edema. Lip scar ok.

Screening/prevention:
- Colonoscopy 2016 normal (old records).
- AAA: ever-smoker male 65-75, ordering one-time abdominal aortic ultrasound.
- Vaccines today: high-dose flu, Shingrix #1, COVID booster. Shingrix #2 in 2-6 months at pharmacy.
- Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids.

Problem list updated: laryngeal cancer moved to history after surgery with negative margins.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Wellness visit labs are back and look fine: kidneys, liver, potassium, blood counts and cholesterol all in range. The aorta ultrasound is set for 10/19.

reports.text: Limited abdominal ultrasound for aortic screening. The abdominal aorta measures up to 2.1 cm in maximal outer-to-outer diameter, without aneurysm. Iliac origins normal in caliber. Visualized liver and kidneys unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: No abdominal aortic aneurysm.

documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OTOLARYNGOLOGY - SURVEILLANCE NOTE
Five months after left partial laryngectomy. Voice slowly improving. No dysphagia, odynophagia or ear pain.
Flexible laryngoscopy: operative site well healed, no mucosal lesion, airway patent. Neck without palpable adenopathy.
No evidence of recurrence. Next scope in 3-4 months; CT neck/chest at one year. Still smoking - counseled.

orders.reason: progressive dyspnea and new leg edema in severe COPD; please see sooner

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Breathing has been sliding since about September. Now winded after one trip to the mailbox. Cough most of the day, yellow-white sputum, no blood, no fever. For two weeks his ankles have been puffy by evening, sock marks. No chest pain. No palpitations or fainting. Using albuterol 4-5 times a day. Still smoking 1 ppd.

O: SpO2 92% on room air at rest. Speaking in full sentences. Neck veins visible at 45 degrees. Lungs: decreased breath sounds, scattered rhonchi, no focal crackles. Heart regular, P2 seems loud. Ankle/pretibial pitting edema bilaterally.

A/P
Progressive dyspnea with new peripheral edema in severe COPD - concern for right heart strain. He has a routine pulmonary appointment in April; called the pulmonary office and they moved him to 3/8. They will get labs, CXR and ECG there. Reviewed warning signs (worse breathing at rest, chest pain, confusion) - ED. Leg elevation. Albuterol as needed.
Again advised stopping smoking.

conditions.label: Cor pulmonale (chronic)
conditions.note: Chronic right heart failure secondary to COPD

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily in the morning

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Lungs hyperinflated with flattened diaphragms. Central pulmonary arteries prominent. No focal consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Cardiac silhouette within normal limits.
reports.conclusion: Hyperinflation consistent with COPD. Prominent pulmonary artery.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 98. Right axis deviation. Tall R wave in V1 with right ventricular strain pattern.
reports.conclusion: Right axis deviation and right ventricular hypertrophy.

documents.title: Pulmonary consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PULMONARY & CRITICAL CARE GROUP - CLINIC LETTER
Visit 3/8/2022

Dear colleague,
I saw Mr. Bianchi, whom we know for severe COPD, earlier than planned. Over six months his breathing has steadily worsened; he has a daily productive cough and in recent weeks swollen legs. No chest pain, palpitations or syncope. History also of lip and laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma, both treated surgically. He smokes about 40 pack-years and continues.

Medications: tiotropium, albuterol, fluticasone/salmeterol. NKDA.

Exam: BP 135/85, HR 98, RR 22, SpO2 92% on room air. Jugular venous distension; P2 is prominent and there is a palpable right ventricular heave. Abdomen soft, liver edge palpable below the costal margin. Pitting edema 2+ of both legs to mid-shin.

Labs: Hgb 15.2, WBC 7.8, platelets 250, BNP 250, creatinine 1.1, AST 40, ALT 35, albumin 3.9, INR 1.0.
CXR: hyperinflation with a prominent pulmonary artery.
ECG: right axis deviation and RVH.

Impression: cor pulmonale - right heart failure due to pulmonary hypertension from his COPD.
Plan:
- Start furosemide 40 mg each morning. BMP in two weeks (we've asked your office to draw it).
- Continue triple inhaled therapy.
- Smoking cessation remains the most important step.
- Return 3 months.

documents.title: Hematology consultation
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY - CONSULT LETTER
Visit 2/20/2023

Reason: erythrocytosis.

69-year-old man with severe COPD (GOLD D), pulmonary hypertension with chronic right heart failure, and previously treated laryngeal and lower lip squamous cell carcinomas. He describes tiredness, headaches, some dizziness and difficulty concentrating. He smokes a pack a day.

Exam: SpO2 89% breathing room air. Breath sounds decreased on both sides; slight cyanosis of the lips. Neurologic exam normal. Spleen not palpable; no lymphadenopathy.

Labs: Hgb 19.0, Hct 57%, MCV 89. Serum erythropoietin elevated (resulted 2/22).

Assessment: secondary polycythemia, driven by chronic hypoxemia (and smoking). The raised EPO and absent splenomegaly argue against a primary marrow process.

Recommendations:

2. Smoking cessation.
3. No phlebotomy for now; will recheck CBC here in about 4 months.

OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Date of service: 3/1/2024

Referred for worsening right heart failure. Over three months: more leg swelling, abdominal fullness and shrinking exercise tolerance. He denies chest pain and orthopnea.

Medications (per patient): tiotropium, albuterol. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: 45 pack-years, still smoking.

Exam: temp 37.2 C, pulse 92, BP 128/76, RR 20. JVD to 8 cm above the sternal angle. Pitting edema to mid-shins bilaterally. Hepatomegaly. Loud P2. Systolic murmur.

ECG: right axis deviation, right bundle branch block.
TTE today: hypertrophied, dilated right ventricle with tricuspid regurgitation; normal LV function.

Impression: cor pulmonale with tricuspid regurgitation secondary to RV dilation; pulmonary hypertension from COPD.
Recommendations: no change in medications from our side. Continue oxygen. Follow with pulmonary. Return as needed.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 9/8/2025 (direct admission from PCP). Discharged 9/13/2025.

Presentation: worsening shortness of breath and swelling of both legs. Long-standing severe COPD with several prior admissions for exacerbations; pulmonary hypertension with chronic right heart failure; tricuspid regurgitation; secondary polycythemia; treated laryngeal and lip SCC.

Exam on admission: elevated jugular venous pressure, pitting edema of both legs, loud pulmonic component of S2, faint crackles at both bases.

Hospital course:
1. COPD exacerbation - doxycycline 100 mg twice daily x5 days and prednisone 40 mg daily x5 days, scheduled nebulizers, oxygen titrated back to his home 2 L.
2. Acute on chronic right heart failure - IV furosemide with good diuresis, transitioned back to furosemide 40 mg by mouth daily at discharge.

Discharge medications: home regimen unchanged (tiotropium, fluticasone/salmeterol, albuterol, furosemide 40 mg daily, oxygen 2 L continuous); antibiotic and prednisone courses completed in hospital.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1-2 weeks; pulmonary as scheduled. Smoking cessation advised.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Transition call after 9/8-9/13 admission. Pt home, breathing "better than before I went in." Weight 2 kg below admission per his scale. Taking furosemide 40 daily and all inhalers, on O2 2 L. Finished the steroid and antibiotic in the hospital. No fever. Follow-up scheduled 9/23 with PCP. Reviewed red flags.

COMMUNITY HOSPITAL ED - PROVIDER NOTE
Seen: 11/4/2025

CC: short of breath, cough, fever.
HPI: 72-year-old man with severe COPD on 2 L home oxygen and cor pulmonale, back with several days of more dyspnea and a cough productive of yellow sputum, with fever. Was admitted in September for a COPD flare and treated with antibiotics and steroids.
Meds: tiotropium, fluticasone/salmeterol, albuterol, furosemide 40 mg, O2 2 L. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: current smoker 1 ppd (45 pack-years); 3-4 drinks most evenings; retired farmer.

Triage: T 38.7 C, HR 102, RR 26, SpO2 89% on room air (portable tank empty on arrival).
Exam: decreased breath sounds with dullness to percussion at the right base.

Labs: leukocytosis with left shift (WBC 16.8, neutrophils 88%, bands reported).
CXR: RLL consolidation, blunted right costophrenic angle.
Thoracentesis (ED, ultrasound-guided): cloudy fluid. pH 7.10; glucose 30; LDH 600 (serum 200); protein 4.5 (serum 7.0); WBC 20,000 with 90% neutrophils; Gram stain gram-positive cocci in clusters.

Assessment: right lower lobe pneumonia with complicated parapneumonic effusion.
ED course: blood cultures, IV vancomycin, oxygen, pulmonary and surgery consulted; chest tube placed. Admitted to medicine.

reports.text: Portable AP view after right chest tube removal. Improving right lower lobe opacity. Small residual blunting at the right base. No pneumothorax.
reports.conclusion: Improving right lower lobe consolidation and effusion; no pneumothorax after tube removal.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: hospitalist

REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 11/4/2025 from the ED. Discharged 11/12/2025.

Diagnoses: right lower lobe pneumonia with complicated parapneumonic effusion. Background severe COPD on home O2, cor pulmonale with tricuspid regurgitation, secondary polycythemia, treated laryngeal and lip SCC.

Course:
- Right chest tube thoracostomy 11/4 with good drainage; tube removed 11/10 with follow-up film showing improvement and no pneumothorax.
- Pleural culture: methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus. Vancomycin narrowed to IV cefazolin 11/7. Defervesced by day 3.
- Oxygen back to baseline 2 L. Diuretic held two days while eating poorly, then resumed at 40 mg.

Discharge medications: cephalexin 500 mg four times daily to complete 4 weeks of total antibiotic therapy (through 12/2); home regimen otherwise unchanged.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: pulmonary clinic with chest x-ray in 3-4 weeks; PCP 1-2 weeks. Strongly advised to stop smoking.
